title: fix(plugin-form,fields): a form neither submits nor offers a field the caller may read but not edit (objectui#10120)
body:
Fixes #10120

Clause-②: no — no exported symbol is added, removed, renamed or retyped, no key on a published payload moves, and no accept set is relaxed. Declared from THIS diff, not from the card: `sanitizeFormData` gains an optional third argument and `fieldWriteGate` / `applyFieldPermissions` are new, but `@object-ui/plugin-form` publishes `.` only, from `index.tsx`, which re-exports neither module. Measured on the built `dist/index.d.ts` with a positive control in the same command: `sanitizeFormData` 0 hits, `fieldWriteGate` / `applyFieldPermissions` 0 hits, `ObjectForm` 6 hits — so the zeros are measured absences, not a silent instrument. `LookupField`'s props are unchanged.

⚠️ The claim comment on the card deliberately carried no `Clause-②:` line (there was no diff yet) and named a `Clause-②-correction:` as the protocol's second carrier. That correction is the seat's to post; this body is the declaration it corrects toward, and its value is `no`.

## What reproduced, and what did not

Everything on the card was relayed. Re-derived here at the seams, on `origin/main` at `afb228418`, with a `reporter` principal whose permission set marks `kpi_entry_line.score` `readable: true, editable: false` — the card's own fixture:

| seam | payload on a save that edited only `actual_value` | the refused field's control |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `ObjectForm` (record page) | `score` already ABSENT | already rendered disabled |
| `ModalForm` (record edit dialog) | `score` already ABSENT | already rendered disabled |
| `DrawerForm` | `score` PRESENT — reproduces | rendered as a live, enabled input |
| `LookupField` chip, field `disabled` | — | trigger disabled, browse disabled, **remove ✕ live** |

⇒ **The card's premise is partly falsified and partly confirmed, and the difference is the finding.** The two console entry points the card names — the record page and the record edit dialog — already carried a field-level strip and a render gate when this branch was cut, so the card's exact reproduction path no longer 403s there. What it was really reporting is a family that disagreed with itself: each container spelled its own COPY of both halves, and the third container of the family carried neither. That is the same defect class as objectui#10108 one layer down, and the drawer is reachable from the same authored `formType` key the other two are.

The lit control the card supplied held at every seam: the unchanged, un-denied columns (`indicator_name`, `target_value`, `weight`) are still on the wire after the fix, so this is not "send less".

## The existing 「may this caller edit this field」 answer, reused

`checkField(object, field, 'write')` in `@object-ui/permissions` — `MePermissionsProvider` resolves it from the server's `/me/permissions` envelope by `"OBJECT.FIELD"` key, falling back to the object-level `allowEdit` for a field no permission set mentions. ⛔ No rung of it is re-derived here. `fieldWriteGate` adapts that one verdict into the predicate the outbound filter takes, and `applyFieldPermissions` into the field-list pass that decides what renders.

## What changed

- The field-level verdict reaches the ONE outbound filter (`sanitizeFormData`'s new `canEdit` option) instead of a strip loop written out after each container's call — the loops were the thing that could be forgotten, and one of three had been.
- One render pass for all three containers. `DrawerForm` gains both halves; `ObjectForm` and `ModalForm` produce the payloads and the markup they produced before.
- Both halves stay fail-open with no permission provider mounted (`isLoaded` false): a standalone form, a designer preview and a guest surface have no resolvable principal, and the server still enforces.
- A lookup's selected chip withholds its remove ✕ when the field is disabled. ⚠️ That is how BOTH of this card's refusals arrive at the widget: a field the object declares `readonly` is folded into `disabled` by the form's section builder, and a field the permission set refuses is marked disabled by the pass above. The chips stay — the value is readable — only the affordance goes.

## Ablation

Committed first, then mutated, then restored from `HEAD`; both mutations verified to have landed on disk by counting the anchor text before and after, and the restore verified byte-identical (`git hash-object` equals the `HEAD` blob for both files, and `git diff HEAD` empty). No `dist/` is involved: the root vitest config aliases every `@object-ui/*` specifier to that package's `src`, so the mutation is what the tests load.

- Remove the `canEdit` branch from `sanitizeFormData` and the chip gate from `LookupField` → **7 failed / 9 passed**, and the seven are exactly the payload rows (all three containers), the two filter rows and the two chip rows.
- Restore → **16 passed**. Every CONTROL row stayed green on both legs, which is what a control has to do.

Direction observed: turn-red, as expected. The two render-gate rows stayed green under this ablation because it does not touch `applyFieldPermissions`; their before-state is the direct measurement in the table above, taken on unmodified `origin/main`.

## Checks on this head

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-form/ packages/fields/` → **280 files, 4001 passed, 1 skipped**, exit 0 (through the shared verify lock).
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form --filter @object-ui/fields type-check` → exit 0. Each package's script is `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the new test files are covered.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form --filter @object-ui/fields lint` → exit 0, 0 errors (906 pre-existing warnings in plugin-form, all `no-explicit-any`; the new files add only that same warning the packages already carry).
- Gates, each exit 0: `check:control-bytes`, `check:changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations), `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`. `check-governed-queue-guard --test` over all nine paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- ⚠️ Declared narrowing: the repo-level scans belong to CI. The shared verify lock was held by a sibling lane for most of this run (two 9-minute queue timeouts on it), so the single-package `vite build` used for the `Clause-②` `.d.ts` measurement was run outside it. Everything reported above is a real reading; nothing is inferred.

## Acceptance notes

Out of scope, seen but left alone by this branch and not filed from it:

- ⛔ Routed elsewhere by the dispatch and deliberately untouched: submitting only DIRTY fields is objectui#10156, and naming the refused field in the 403 instead of the console's generic message is owned by the producing side. Neither is addressed here; both remain open.
- `LineItemsPanel` — the child-row grid inside a master-detail form — consults no field-level permission at all when it decides which cells are editable. Not measured on this branch and not filed from it; the outbound half is partly covered already, because a master-detail child update sends only the cells that differ. Handed to the report for the triage seat to dedupe and file.
- The outer schema gate in `ObjectFormRenderer` no-ops on a `fields` entry that is a bare string rather than an object, which is the shape the console's global record form passes. Harmless today — every container re-applies the same pass to the resolved field list downstream, which is what covers that path — so it is an observation, not a defect. Noted, not filed. Successor: whoever unifies that outer gate with the per-container one.
